court: High Court of Judicature at Madras

case_name: Smt. Kavitha v. Smt. Rukmini — full case name
facts_of_case: The parties were married under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The wife claimed that her husband had deserted her and sought divorce. The trial court allowed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: A petition for divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is maintainable only if it is proved that the respondent has been guilty of adultery.
legal_principles.held: It is held that a petition for divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is maintainable only if it is proved that the respondent has been guilty of adultery. The burden lies on the petitioner to prove this fact beyond reasonable doubt.
use_in: divorce cases under Hindu Marriage Act

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the petitioner to prove that the respondent has been guilty of adultery beyond reasonable doubt.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that the burden lies on the petitioner to prove that the respondent has been guilty of adultery beyond reasonable doubt.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 — Section X
use_in: divorce cases under Hindu Marriage Act

outcome.final_order: The final order was to dismiss the appeal and uphold the decision of the trial court.
